Blind: MAB Conflict_Resolution and ConvoMem wired as V03 (run_blind_validation.sh, blind_split_*.json) but never run. PrefEval downloaded, not wired. LongMemEval excluded by owner decision.
others: MemMachine and Nemori: LoCoMo cat 1-4 only, cat 5 skipped. Cognee: vendor LoCoMo plus BEAM with settings chosen on the reported questions. Honcho: open harness for LoCoMo, LongMemEval and BEAM, single vendor run.

options.label: Today: two dev, two blind, PrefEval later
options.detail: LoCoMo and OP-Bench drive design; MAB-CR and ConvoMem only confirm; PrefEval stays a non-blocking shape check.
options.note: Preference adherence is never a gate, so a personalisation regression can pass.

options.label: Five-set suite with PrefEval blind
options.detail: Dev: LoCoMo (with cat 5) and OP-Bench. Blind gates: MAB-CR, ConvoMem and PrefEval, each sealed by hash split and run once per frozen candidate.
options.note: Covers recall, over-personalisation, conflict update, multi-shape chat and preference following.

options.label: Rotate dev and blind roles
options.detail: Each release swaps which sets are dev and which are blind, so no set is tuned on forever.
options.note: Once a blind set is inspected it cannot be sealed again; rotation burns sets.

options.label: B plus dataset-free behavioural suite as a gate
options.detail: As B, and the metamorphic control suite (G-04) counts as a sixth, dataset-free gate.
options.note: Guards generic behaviour that no benchmark covers.

why: Owner scope (LoCoMo+cat5, OP-Bench, MAB-CR, ConvoMem, PrefEval; no LongMemEval) plus GAP_TO_SOLUTION_PLAN rule 7 and rule 8. Making PrefEval blind adds the only preference-following signal; the behavioural suite catches benchmark-specific wins that do not generalise.
owner_note: Standing owner decision: LongMemEval stays out of the suite.

title: Uncertainty and noise band method
question: How should v2 decide that a paired difference is larger than noise?
today: One global rule band = 0.328*sqrt(n) questions (eval_blind.py:59, eval_screen.py), derived from one 233-question repeat (A16); accuracy_ci gives a conversation cluster bootstrap in every summary (A10); evals/noise_floor.py exists but waits for two same-config repeat runs per slice (I16).
others: MIRIX: three runs with per-run spread. LightMem: two judges, single run, no variance. Mem0: a stated +-1 judge interval only. Hindsight: no interval.

options.label: Keep the global sqrt(n) band
options.detail: One coefficient for every dataset and slice.
options.note: Codex review: 0.328 is not per dataset; OP-Bench and MAB flip rates differ.

options.label: Per-dataset cluster bootstrap
options.detail: Paired bootstrap resampling conversations (or personas) per dataset, report a 95% interval of the paired difference plus an exact sign test on flips.
options.note: Right unit of dependence; CPU only.

options.label: B calibrated by repeat runs
options.detail: As B, and each dataset's band is checked against two same-configuration repeat runs (flip rate), taking the wider of the two.
options.note: Includes reader and judge nondeterminism, not only sampling error.

options.label: Bayesian hierarchical model
options.detail: Item-level model with conversation and category effects giving posterior probability of improvement per slice.
options.note: Harder to explain in a paper and to audit.

why: A10 and I16: the code for B exists; G-E1 asks for per-conversation bootstrap per dataset; RV12 asks for repeated null controls. One repeat run per dataset is a small, one-off GPU cost.

title: Metamorphic and behavioural controls
question: Which dataset-free behavioural controls should every v2 change pass, and do they block adoption?
today: Planned in GAP_TO_SOLUTION_PLAN.md rule 8 (name swap, speaker-order swap, entity renaming, paraphrase, filler insertion, generic vs personal requests, unanswerable questions, tenant pairs) but NOT built (V01 'behavioural control suite not built'); only the I19 multi-user leakage probe exists.
others: No surveyed engine ships metamorphic controls. Honcho and MemMachine test isolation by scope keys only; Mnemon re-reads shown items from the source before publishing (a consistency check, not a control).

options.label: No suite; rely on benchmarks
options.detail: Keep today's state.
options.note: Benchmark-shaped rules (date wording, speaker names) pass unnoticed.

options.label: Invariance suite, report only
options.detail: Synthetic generated conversations (Ilse, Bram) with renaming, paraphrase, order swap and filler; answers must be invariant; results printed but not blocking.
options.note: Visibility without teeth.

options.label: Invariance plus safety pairs, blocking
options.detail: As B, plus tenant-isolation pairs, unanswerable probes and generic-vs-personal requests; any change whose answers flip under a pure renaming, or that leaks across a tenant pair, is rejected.
options.note: Retrieval-only variants run on CPU; reader variants need a small model budget.

options.label: C plus property-based fuzzing of the store
options.detail: As C, and hypothesis-style generators drive write/correct/forget sequences, checking invariants (no resurrection after forget, supersede keeps history, trust never rises along lineage).
options.note: Finds state bugs benchmarks never touch; more test engineering.

why: Plan rule 8 and V01 make this the dataset-free guard against overfitting; the brief requires generic behaviour. D's store fuzzing is valuable but can grow in later as part of G-13 erasure and G-08 lineage tests.

title: Loop-level metrics in the v2 harness
question: Which of the five loop metrics (loop gain, drift fidelity, correction latency, forgetting compliance, cost per cycle) must v2 measure, and on what protocol?
today: Only cost_per_cycle exists (evals/memspine_evals/metrics.py:128; evals/README.md 'cost_per_cycle' splits query and build tokens and states snapshot QA is not the episode metric). Loop gain, drift fidelity, correction latency and forgetting compliance are defined in the paper but not computed.
others: LightMem and Nemori: per-stage call and token accounting. Honcho: per-call token telemetry. No surveyed engine reports a multi-session loop metric; all publish snapshot QA.

options.label: Cost per cycle only
options.detail: Keep today's snapshot-QA cost split.
options.note: The paper's central loop claims stay unmeasured.

options.label: Cheap scripted episode protocol
options.detail: Scripted multi-session episodes (Ilse changes job, Bram asks to forget an address) run through the real write/read loop; compute correction latency (turns until a correction is reflected) and forgetting compliance (residual hits after forget) on CPU with a retrieval-only check.
options.note: Two metrics, deterministic, no model cost.

options.label: All five on a replayed-session protocol
options.detail: As B, plus loop gain (per-user utility slope over sessions) and drift fidelity (profile tracking a scripted preference drift), using a small reader budget; cost per cycle measured on the same live episodes.
options.note: Gives the paper its loop evidence; loop gain needs a utility judge.

options.label: C plus metrics as adoption guards
options.detail: As C, and forgetting compliance and correction latency become non-inferiority guards in G-01, with cost per cycle carrying a predeclared tolerance (plan rule 9).
options.note: A recall gain that slows corrections or leaks forgotten content is blocked.

why: CLAUDE.md lists the five metrics as MemSpine-owned constructs; RV10 and plan rule 9 require cost reported with quality; forgetting compliance is also the erasure test of G-13. B is the minimum if GPU time is short.

title: Memory firewall default posture
question: Which write-time firewall signals are on by default in v2, and how are chat-shaped false positives handled?
today: firewall.enabled true; default signals instruction regex, embedding outlier and MINJA 96-char prefix bridge (config/schema.py:1376-1407; core/firewall.py); extended instruction, semantic_risk and query_anomaly off (ADR-058). Templated assistant openers trip the bridge (39/40 quarantined on a synthetic chat), fixed only by opt-in minja_bridge_exempt_roles (I21).
others: Hindsight: opt-in Memory Defense, off by default, only a 46-pattern sensitive-data rule. Honcho: structural tag neutralisation only. MemOS: strips recalled-memory blocks before preference extraction. Mem0, Cognee, MIRIX, EverMemOS: none.

options.label: Today: three signals, exemptions opt-in
options.detail: Keep the current defaults; chat deployments must know to exempt the assistant role.
options.note: Safe, but quarantines legitimate assistant turns on chat data.

options.label: Role-aware defaults
options.detail: Bridge and outlier signals apply to external and tool channels by default; the assistant role keeps instruction patterns but is exempt from the prefix bridge; an operator can tighten.
options.note: Removes the main false positive; slightly weaker against assistant-channel injection.

options.label: B plus extended and semantic signals on
options.detail: As B, with instruction_extended and semantic_risk (self-claimed authority, future-answer binding) on by default; query_anomaly stays opt-in.
options.note: Deterministic and cheap; needs a measured false-positive rate on generic chat.

options.label: Model-based injection classifier
options.detail: Add an optional small classifier at write behind a flag, never the only signal.
options.note: Breaks the 'no model in the defence' property (the classifier can itself be attacked).

why: N1 rests on a deterministic, uninjectable defence (RESEARCH_NOVELTY N1); I21 measured the chat false positive; ADR-058 built the extra signals. Adopt C only after a false-positive screen on the behavioural suite (G-04), else fall back to B.

title: Cross-agent reach bound by default
question: When memory is shared across agents or principals, should the trust-horizon invariant (attenuation per grant hop) be on by default?
today: integrity.enabled false in schema and base (config/schema.py:1458; core/integrity.py), on in templates/multi_agent.yaml:21-22 with kappa 0.5; off means foreign records get a flat TRUST_RETRIEVED_CAP 0.3 and trust-blind ranking. Reported LLM-study numbers use declared parents with harness-side admission; enforcement-on reruns queued (RESEARCH_NOVELTY N1 status).
others: Cognee: dataset share permission, no reach bound. MIRIX: client read/write scopes, vault retrieve path ignores scopes. Hindsight: shared banks and tags, no trust decay. MemOS: readable/writable cube lists, no per-record trust.

options.label: Flat cap, invariant opt-in
options.detail: Today: foreign records capped at 0.3; THI only in the multi_agent template.
options.note: Single-user deployments pay nothing; shared ones need to pick the template.

options.label: Invariant on whenever a grant exists
options.detail: THI switches on automatically the moment any cross-namespace grant is created; single-namespace use is unchanged.
options.note: Bound holds in every shared deployment without the user knowing the flag.

options.label: B plus live re-evaluation
options.detail: As B, and each candidate's trust is rechecked against current parents at read (live_reevaluation), so quarantine, rollback or grant revocation propagate.
options.note: Extra storage reads per candidate; radii only shrink.

options.label: Scope-only isolation, no trust arithmetic
options.detail: Drop trust attenuation; rely on grant scopes like peers.
options.note: Gives up the N1 claim.

why: N1 is D-1's strongest claim and it is only true in deployments that turn THI on; B makes the claim hold by construction for every shared store. C adds cost per read and can graduate later via G-22 once its latency is measured.

title: Lineage enforcement for derived records
question: How does v2 guarantee that every derived record names its parents, so trust and erasure can follow lineage?
today: Engine-made derivations (summaries, window facts, lead blocks) take the minimum parent trust (survey memspine trust.provenance); caller writes may pass derived_from. integrity.implicit_parents defaults 'off' (config/schema.py:1458+), so an agent can read and then write without declared parents and launder trust.
others: Honcho: derived conclusions must cite existing ids, invented ids discarded. Hindsight: observations carry source_memory_ids and proof counts. MemMachine: citations kept on profile features. Mem0: no link from a memory to its source turn.

options.label: Declared parents only
options.detail: Today: caller declares derived_from; engine derivations self-declare.
options.note: Agent writes after a read can omit lineage.

options.label: Implicit parents per turn by default
options.detail: The engine records what a session read and attaches it as parents to that turn's next agent-channel write (implicit_parents=turn).
options.note: May over-attach parents and lower trust of genuinely new user facts written by the agent.

options.label: Implicit parents per session
options.detail: Read ledger kept until end_session; every later write inherits it.
options.note: Strongest containment, broadest trust lowering.

options.label: Span-level evidence per assertion
options.detail: Each derived assertion stores evidence spans per endpoint (RV02) plus parents; lineage and citation become the same object.
options.note: Shared with the write-path area's assertion envelope; larger records.

why: B0 made implicit parents available; RV07 and RV21 show erasure and cache lineage depend on complete parent sets. B on the agent/tool channel only keeps user-direct writes unaffected; D belongs to the write-path area's envelope decision.

title: Low-trust content in the context window
question: How should records below a trust threshold be shown to the generator at compose time?
today: integrity.untrusted_wrap_below 0.0 and claims_only_below 0.0 (both off; config/schema.py IntegrityConfig B6/B9); quarantined records never reach search or assemble; instruction-flagged records are stored inert.
others: Memori: facts injected in a <memori_context> tag with one hedge sentence. Mnemon: read-side rubric says notes are data, never instructions. Honcho: neutralises message tags. Mem0: raw text, no wrapper.

options.label: Raw text, quarantine only
options.detail: Today: anything not quarantined is rendered as plain text.
options.note: Instruction framing in tool or external content reaches the reader verbatim.

options.label: Untrusted-data wrapper below a threshold
options.detail: Records whose view trust is below a fixed cut are rendered inside a labelled 'data, not instructions' block.
options.note: Cheap; relies on the reader obeying the label.

options.label: Claims-only below a threshold
options.detail: Raw low-trust text never enters the window; only its mined atomic facts appear, marked unverified.
options.note: Strong containment; loses nuance when mining is incomplete.

options.label: B by default, C in protected profiles
options.detail: Wrapper on in every profile at the external-channel cap; claims-only on in protected and regulated templates.
options.note: Profile-scoped default per flag graduation.

why: B6 and B9 are built and default off; the wrapper has no recall cost while claims-only trades recall for containment, so it belongs in profiles that ask for containment (plan rule 10: default inside a data-shape profile).

title: PII and secret handling default
question: What should v2 do by default with secrets, PII and sensitive topics at write, and with their text in prompts to remote models?
today: firewall.redact_secrets false, pii 'off', pii_extended false, sensitive_topics false (config/schema.py:1407+); consent.remote_llm_max_tier None (no remote gate); multi_agent and regulated_financial templates set redact_secrets true and pii redact. Default stack is local (fastembed, no LLM role bound).
others: Hindsight: opt-in 46-pattern sensitive-data rule. MIRIX: vault stores credentials with a sensitivity label but in plain columns and returns them from search. Memori: BYODB hashes ids but sends message content in plain text to its hosted extractor. Mem0: none, PostHog telemetry on by default.

options.label: Off by default, templates opt in
options.detail: Today.
options.note: A user who binds a hosted model leaks whatever was stored.

options.label: Redact secrets always, tag PII
options.detail: Secrets (keys, tokens, private keys) redacted by default; PII tagged (pii:<kind>, raised pii_tier) but text kept; sensitive topics tagged.
options.note: Secrets are never useful memory; PII may be (Ilse's own address).

options.label: B plus remote-model tier gate
options.detail: As B, and records above a PII tier are withheld from any prompt sent to a non-local provider (remote_llm_max_tier=low by default); local hosts unaffected.
options.note: Hosted users lose some recall on personal details until they opt in.

options.label: Redact all PII by default
options.detail: Replace PII matches with [REDACTED:<kind>] at write.
options.note: Destroys legitimate personal memory (phone numbers the user asked to keep).

why: Deterministic checksummed patterns (#44, N23) cost nothing; the risk is concentrated at the remote-model boundary, which is where C acts. BD-5 keeps extraction local by design, so C only bites when a user binds a hosted model.

title: Consent and purpose scopes
question: Should v2 records carry a purpose set that reads must match, and what happens to untagged records?
today: consent.enforce false, untagged 'allow' (config/schema.py:1620); write(..., purposes=[...]) sets consent_tags; derived records inherit consent (core/privacy.py inherited_consent); the REST middleware sets the read purpose.
others: Cognee: per-dataset ACL (read, write, delete, share), no purpose model. Honcho: per-peer observe_me switches what is derived, no purpose tags. Hindsight: retain_mission narrows extraction; tag-scoped visibility. Mem0, MemMachine: none.

options.label: Opt-in purpose enforcement
options.detail: Today: tags recorded, enforcement off.
options.note: Zero friction; purpose limitation is a paper feature, not a default.

options.label: Do-not-derive consent instead of purposes
options.detail: Replace purposes with per-subject switches: store raw but do not derive profile/facts about a subject who opted out.
options.note: Simpler, covers the common 'don't profile me' case; no purpose limitation.

options.label: Purposes plus do-not-derive
options.detail: Keep purpose tags (opt-in enforcement) and add a subject-level do-not-derive switch that K_P and K_C must honour, on by default when set.
options.note: Covers both regulated deployments and personal assistants.

options.label: Enforce purposes by default, untagged deny
options.detail: Every read must state a purpose; untagged records invisible.
options.note: Breaks every caller that does not tag.

why: #50 purpose limitation is built and inheritance through lineage works; the missing piece for a personal assistant is a per-subject 'do not profile' that K_P honours (impact order O3 systemic changes need a user control). Enforcement-by-default stays a regulated-profile setting.

title: Isolation boundary and multi-party visibility
question: What is the hard isolation unit in v2 and how is visibility inside it expressed?
today: Hierarchical namespace is the single enforcement point (core/namespace.py validate_namespace, grant_allows); inside a namespace I53 participant and visibility tags (private, participants, owner_shared) with an optional viewer predicate (core/visibility.py); derived records inherit the strictest visibility. ADR-065 isolation work; I19 leakage probe found no leak in 12 configs.
others: Hindsight: bank per user/agent, Postgres schema per tenant, tags inside. Honcho: workspace > peer > session with (observer, observed) collections. MIRIX: org > client > user with write_scope/read_scopes. EverMemOS: row key omits app/project (conditional overwrite risk, RV21).

options.label: Namespace plus visibility tags
options.detail: Today: one path-shaped namespace boundary, tag-based visibility inside.
options.note: Tags are soft; any reader that forgets the viewer predicate sees everything.

options.label: Namespace plus mandatory viewer
options.detail: As A, but every read inside a multi-party namespace must name a viewer; reads without one see only owner_shared and unmarked records.
options.note: Fail closed for group chats and household assistants.

options.label: Observer-observed collections
options.detail: Store a separate view per (observer, observed) pair inside a namespace.
options.note: Theory-of-mind views; duplicates derived state per observer.

options.label: Physical store per tenant
options.detail: Separate database or schema per top-level tenant, namespaces inside.
options.note: Strongest at the server edge; heavier operations.

why: RV21 asks for isolation tests over write/search/update/delete and cache hits; B keeps one enforcement point and makes multi-party reads fail closed. D can be an optional server deployment setting (G-19) rather than the data model.

title: Right to erasure across derived state
question: What must a v2 erasure remove, and how is that proved?
today: forget is soft by default; hard=True cascades through source.parents and consolidation members, redacts event payloads (core/erasure.py redact_record, retained_fields), purges embedding and extraction caches and window replies, cleans LanceDB versions, checkpoints the WAL (engine.py:9657-9697,9822-9860); erase_subject (9699), erase_namespace (9731), verify_forget. RV07: reply-to-source cache membership is process-local and can be outlived by a persistent cache.
others: Hindsight: delete cascades to derived observations; survivors reset for re-consolidation. MemMachine: profile features derived from a deleted episode survive. Mem0: history row keeps deleted text. MemOS: no cascade into copies in other nodes' sources. Cognee: forget removes derived graph/vector artefacts under a dataset lock.

options.label: Today: soft default, hard cascade on request
options.detail: Keep the current verbs and verify_forget.
options.note: Cache lineage gap across restarts (RV07) remains.

options.label: A plus persisted reverse lineage for caches
options.detail: Every cache entry and derived projection (vectors, lexical index, graph edges, window replies, profile) records its source ids and generation; erasure tombstones them and a generation check stops stale publication of an in-flight derivation.
options.note: Closes restart and in-flight races; more bookkeeping on every derivation.

options.label: B plus re-derivation of survivors
options.detail: As B, and a summary or profile that had the erased record among several parents is re-derived from the remaining parents rather than deleted whole.
options.note: Keeps useful summaries; costs model calls after each erasure.

options.label: Crypto-shredding per subject
options.detail: Encrypt each subject's payloads with a per-subject key and erase by destroying the key, including in backups.
options.note: Covers backups and logs; key management burden.

why: RV07 and RV21: an erasure path does not certify caches and derived views; the gate is absence of retained payloads after restart and during inference. Re-derivation keeps summaries useful and matches the forgetting-compliance metric (G-05). D can follow later for backup coverage.

title: Retention policy and event log lifetime
question: What retention behaviour should v2 ship by default for the event log and for memory records?
today: event_log.mode FULL (append-only forever) with ROLLING and EPHEMERAL modes (core/events.py:33; D-45, N2); retention.classes empty, so nothing expires (config/schema.py:1575); per-type may_delete and legal holds respected by the sleep-cycle expiry stage.
others: Cognee: session tier TTL 7 days swept every 15 minutes. MemOS: capacity caps per memory type with eviction at 80%. Mem0: per-memory expiration_date hides rows. Honcho: errored queue items kept 30 days; no memory TTL.

options.label: Full log, no expiry
options.detail: Today's default.
options.note: Full audit and rebuild; unbounded growth and storage limitation is the user's job.

options.label: Full log, working-memory TTL
options.detail: Keep the full log; ship one default class: working and session-scoped records expire after a fixed TTL; long-term types never expire automatically.
options.note: Bounds scratch growth without touching personal memory.

options.label: Rolling log by default
options.detail: Prune applied events past a window; rebuild and taint audit limited to the window.
options.note: Weakens audit taint and migration by replay (G-23).

options.label: Profile-specific retention
options.detail: Retention class set per template (assistant: B; regulated: explicit TTLs and FULL log; coding: rolling); no global default.
options.note: Right default per workload; more to document.

why: N2 claims a retention-mode spectrum, which is best shown as profile defaults; the FULL log stays the default for chat because migration by replay (G-23) and audit taint (G-15) depend on it.

title: Audit log scope and default
question: What does v2 audit by default, and is the audit trail tamper-evident?
today: audit.reads false, audit.actions false (config/schema.py:1587); when on, memory.read_audit / memory.audit events carry a hash chain checked by Engine.audit_chain_ok (core/privacy.py); audit taint walks the event log for blast radius (core/audit.py trace_taint); agent tool calls always log a line (protocols/tools.py).
others: Hindsight: audit log off by default; manual curation with revert. Mem0: history table logs ADD/UPDATE/DELETE with actor and keeps deleted text. Honcho: per-call telemetry, no tamper evidence. Cognee: provenance stamping task off by default.

options.label: Off by default
options.detail: Today.
options.note: Taint audit still works from the mutation log; no record of who read what.

options.label: Actions on, reads off
options.detail: forget, correct, erase, export, grant and retention expiry always append a chained memory.audit event; read audit opt-in.
options.note: Low volume; every destructive act is attributable.

options.label: Actions and reads on
options.detail: As B, plus every search/assemble appends returned record ids and purpose.
options.note: Log grows with reads; needed for subject-access requests about disclosure.

options.label: B by default, C in shared and regulated profiles
options.detail: Profile-scoped: personal and assistant get B, multi_agent and regulated get C.
options.note: Matches cost to need.

why: #49 is built and cheap for actions; read audit is the expensive half and matters only where several principals read. An erasure audit event must not itself retain the erased content (RV21), so B's events carry ids and reasons only.

title: Shape of the public Python API
question: What public API surface should v2 expose over the engine?
today: One Engine facade (D-01) in a 15,179-line src/memspine/engine.py with about 114 public methods (write, write_ex, write_messages, search, assemble, retrieve, read, correct, forget, erase_subject, export, sleep, describe, usage, write_timers, structured_stats and many more).
others: Cognee: a handful of verbs (add, cognify, remember, recall, search, forget, prune). Mem0: add / search / get_all / update / delete / history. Hindsight: retain / recall / reflect per bank. Honcho: workspace, peer, session objects with messages and a chat (dialectic) call.

options.label: Keep the single wide facade
options.detail: All verbs stay on Engine; add new ones there.
options.note: Discoverability and reviewability suffer; every feature widens one class.

options.label: Small loop-verb core plus namespaced admin
options.detail: A stable core of loop verbs (remember / recall / compose / correct / forget / sleep) and grouped sub-APIs (engine.admin, engine.privacy, engine.audit, engine.shared, engine.diagnostics); Engine becomes a thin facade over modules.
options.note: Clear stability contract; one refactor and deprecation cycle.

options.label: Object API (session/peer handles)
options.detail: Users obtain a namespace or session handle that carries principal, purpose and viewer; verbs live on the handle.
options.note: Scoping errors become hard to make; bigger change for current callers.

options.label: B with C-style scoped handles
options.detail: Loop-verb core exposed on a scoped handle (namespace, principal, purpose, viewer fixed at creation); admin groups stay on the engine.
options.note: Combines a small surface with fail-closed scoping (G-12).

why: The tool layer already fixes namespace/principal/session in a ToolContext (protocols/tools.py); generalising that to the Python API removes the class of scope mistakes RV21 warns about, and splitting the 15k-line facade is needed for RV06-style refactors anyway.

title: Remote protocols and default authentication
question: Which remote protocols does v2 ship, and what authentication do they require by default?
today: Optional FastAPI REST app (protocols/rest/app.py, 31 routes) with rest.auth.mode default 'none' (config/schema.py RestAuthConfig), reference api_key (HMAC, namespace globs) and oidc_jwt modes; zero-dependency stdio MCP server (protocols/mcp.py) serving the five-tool set with namespace/principal fixed at start-up; every tool write lands on the trust-capped agent_tool channel.
others: Honcho: scoped JWT (admin/workspace/peer/session), USE_AUTH false in self-host. Mem0 server: JWT and API keys but principal not bound to user_id, so any key reaches any scope. MemOS: API keys only when AUTH_ENABLED. EverMemOS: no auth, binds 127.0.0.1.

options.label: Auth none by default
options.detail: Today: operator must configure auth.
options.note: An exposed REST server is open to every namespace.

options.label: Loopback-only unless auth set
options.detail: With mode none the REST server refuses to bind anything but 127.0.0.1; any other bind requires api_key or oidc_jwt; MCP stays stdio.
options.note: Zero setup locally, safe by default when exposed.

options.label: B plus principal-bound scopes
options.detail: As B, and each credential's principal and namespace globs are the only scopes it can name (never a request field), mirrored for MCP over HTTP.
options.note: Prevents Mem0's unbound-principal defect.

options.label: Add MCP over streamable HTTP
options.detail: C plus a remote MCP transport with the same credential binding, for hosted agents.
options.note: Broader reach; one more transport to secure.

why: #51 built api_key namespace globs already; binding refusal is a few lines and closes the default-open server. Remote MCP (D) can follow when a user needs it.

title: Framework adapters (I70)
question: How, and when, should v2 integrate with agent frameworks such as LangGraph, LlamaIndex and OpenAI Agents?
today: None. I70 (optional adapters on the I65 tool dispatcher) is on hold by the owner (GAP_TO_SOLUTION_PLAN.md:15,165); agents integrate through the Python Engine, REST, or the five MCP tools.
others: MemMachine: integrations for LangChain, LangGraph, CrewAI, LlamaIndex, Strands, n8n, Dify. Memori: monkey-patches LLM clients (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Bedrock, LangChain, Agno, Pydantic-AI). Zep and Hindsight: adapters as separate optional packages.

options.label: Stay on hold; MCP is the adapter
options.detail: Rely on MCP plus the Python API.
options.note: Smallest surface; some frameworks need native store interfaces.

options.label: Two thin optional extras
options.detail: LangGraph BaseStore and OpenAI Agents Session adapters as lazy-import extras built only on the tool dispatcher, so all guards apply.
options.note: Adoption help without new trust paths.

options.label: Broad integration catalogue
options.detail: Adapters for most popular frameworks and no-code tools.
options.note: Maintenance load grows with every framework release.

options.label: Client wrapping
options.detail: Wrap LLM clients to write and recall implicitly.
options.note: Invisible writes bypass the explicit consent and channel model.

why: The owner put I70 on hold and it has no evaluation effect (FRAMEWORK_TOOLCALL_SURVEY.md 4.7); keep it in v2 'later' with B as the shape when revived, so adapters can never bypass the dispatcher guards.

title: Deployment modes and background runners
question: Which deployment modes does v2 support as first-class, and which background runner is the default?
today: Embeddable async library by default with optional REST server and stdio MCP; storage sqlite (default) or postgres (config/schema.py:79); workers.runner 'inline' default with dbos and taskiq extras (config/schema.py:265); EPHEMERAL event log for no-persistence use; window extraction queue is process-local (G-W27, RV01).
others: Hindsight: server plus worker, Docker, Helm, embedded pg0 bundle and a local daemon. Honcho: API process and separate deriver workers sharing Postgres. Cognee: library, server, MCP and cloud. Mnemon: research plugins, no product deployment.

options.label: Library-first, inline runner
options.detail: Today's default; servers and durable runners are extras.
options.note: Derived work is lost on crash (RV01).

options.label: Library-first with durable local outbox
options.detail: Same embedded default, but derived work is persisted in the same SQLite store (outbox with leases) so restarts resume it; dbos/taskiq remain for multi-instance.
options.note: Durability with no extra service.

options.label: Three named modes
options.detail: B plus documented, tested modes: embedded (library), server (REST/MCP with Postgres and a worker process), ephemeral (in-memory, no log, for tests and privacy-first sessions); each with its own template.
options.note: Clear support matrix; three CI lanes.

options.label: Server-first
options.detail: Make the REST server and a worker the primary product; library becomes a client.
options.note: Loses the zero-infrastructure embedded story.

why: RV01/G-W27 require durable derivation regardless of mode; naming three modes makes the ephemeral privacy mode (N2) and the server mode testable claims instead of configuration folklore.

title: Observability, stats and telemetry
question: What runtime observability does v2 provide, and does any of it leave the machine?
today: Engine.describe(), usage() per role, structured_stats() per prompt (repair/failure rates), opt-in write_timers (observability.write_timers, config/schema.py:1606), window_stats counters for call 1 only (G-W13); structlog logging; no OpenTelemetry; no product telemetry (posthog rejected in ECOSYSTEM_METHODOLOGY).
others: Mem0: anonymous PostHog telemetry on by default. Graphiti: optional OpenTelemetry tracing extra. EverMemOS: telemetry span content capture off by default. LightMem and Nemori: per-stage call/token accounting; Honcho: per-call token telemetry.

options.label: In-process stats only
options.detail: Today: pull-style counters and opt-in timers.
options.note: Derived layers lack failure and grounding counters.

options.label: Uniform per-layer ledger
options.detail: Every loop stage and derived layer reports calls, tokens (prompt/completion/cached), retries, failures, dropped coverage and p50/p95 through one stats object.
options.note: Feeds cost per cycle (G-05) and RV10 manifests.

options.label: B plus optional OpenTelemetry export
options.detail: As B, with an optional OTel extra emitting spans and metrics; content never included in spans (ids and counts only).
options.note: Fits server deployments; one more extra.

options.label: Product telemetry by default
options.detail: Anonymous usage pings to the maintainers.
options.note: Conflicts with the local-first privacy stance.

why: G-W13 asks for the same counters on every derived layer; RV10/RV11 need retries, queue delay and dropped coverage recorded; OTel stays an optional extra under D-03 and spans never carry memory text.

title: Defaults policy and configuration profiles
question: What principle decides v2 defaults, and how many profiles carry them?
today: D-03 slim core, no model role bound by default (LLMConfig roles empty, config/schema.py:232); DEFAULT_TEMPLATE 'assistant' (config/constants.py:548, ADR-032); base.yaml carries read settings measured on paid LoCoMo ablations (combo-A, ADR-033); 11 templates (core, base, assistant, benchmark, coding, graph, multi_agent, personal, protected, regulated_financial, voice) plus 7 data-shape presets.
others: Cognee: hosted OpenAI by default, auto-falls back to a local GLiNER extractor and fastembed without a key. Mem0, Honcho, MemMachine: hosted models by default. Hindsight: local embedder and reranker, hosted LLM by default.

options.label: Today: no model, benchmark-measured base
options.detail: Keep D-03 and the combo-A read defaults in base.
options.note: Defaults were chosen on one benchmark's shape (dated chat).

options.label: No model; generic base, shaped presets
options.detail: Keep D-03; base contains only settings that passed every in-scope set and the behavioural suite; shape-specific settings (dated turns, named speakers) move to presets selected by data shape.
options.note: Some measured gains become opt-in until they pass blind sets.

options.label: Local small model by default
options.detail: Bind a small local model for extraction by default when hardware allows.
options.note: Heavy install and hardware detection; violates D-03.

options.label: Hosted model with local fallback
options.detail: Use a hosted LLM when a key exists, else local rules.
options.note: Silent data egress based on an environment variable.

why: D-03 is validated by the ecosystem (DEPENDENCY_ANALYSIS) and BD-5 keeps extraction local; the brief requires generic defaults, and plan rule 10 says global defaults only when every profile benefits, so benchmark-shaped settings belong in presets.

title: Flag graduation and flag retirement
question: How do v2 configuration flags move from opt-in to default, and when are they removed?
today: About 428 schema fields, 242 of them in ReadConfig alone (config/schema.py:288-1332); plan rule 10 defines opt-in -> screened -> candidate -> profile default -> global default, recorded by hand in GAP_REGISTER (759 lines); measured-negative features (word-vector leg, B15) stay as opt-in flags; I69 notes stale extras in uv.lock.
others: Honcho: per-workspace/session/peer config toggles, no graduation rule. Cognee: 30+ extras, IMPROVE_AUTO_ENABLED default true. Mem0: flat config. No surveyed engine documents a graduation rule.

options.label: Keep every flag, graduate by hand
options.detail: Today.
options.note: Untested flag combinations multiply; dead flags rot.

options.label: Machine-readable flag registry
options.detail: Each flag carries status (experimental, screened, candidate, profile-default, default, deprecated), the evidence id and the profile list; describe() and CI read it; a release cannot ship a default whose status lacks evidence.
options.note: Makes rule 10 enforceable; small build.

options.label: B plus retirement budget
options.detail: As B, and a flag measured negative or unscreened for two releases is deprecated and then removed (config migration warns); v2 starts by cutting measured-negative flags.
options.note: Smaller surface; experiments must be re-added to revisit.

options.label: Move experiments to a plugin package
options.detail: Core keeps only graduated behaviour; experimental features live in an experiments extra with their own flags.
options.note: Clean core; cross-package refactor.

why: Plan rule 10 exists only as prose; RV16 shows statuses age and a hook is not an implementation. A registry plus retirement keeps v2's configuration testable and lets the paper cite which behaviour is default with evidence.

title: Backwards compatibility and migration from v1
question: How do existing v1 stores and callers move to v2?
today: Event schema_version 1 on every event (core/events.py:122); SQLite read model migrated in place by Alembic revisions 0001-0005 (services/storage/sqlite/alembic/versions); projectors replay from high-water marks; RV05 needs versioned edge keys with old-key aliases; ADR-064 moves the graph default to LadybugDB.
others: MemOS: memory versioning with soft delete and recover. Mem0 and Honcho: in-place SQL migrations only. Hindsight: export/import/clone of banks. Mnemon: versioned View republished from sources.

options.label: In-place migrations only
options.detail: Alembic revisions on the read model; events untouched; old derived records kept as is.
options.note: v1 derived records (old keys, old fact shapes) linger beside v2 ones.

options.label: Rebuild projections by replay
options.detail: Keep the v1 event log as truth, upcast old event versions on read, and rebuild every v2 projection (vectors, graph, facts) by replay into a fresh store; old derived records are regenerated, never mixed.
options.note: Uses the event-sourced design; derived re-extraction costs model calls.

options.label: B with dual-read period
options.detail: As B, with the v1 store readable through a compatibility shim and deprecation warnings on v1 API names for one minor release.
options.note: Smooth for callers; two code paths for a release.

options.label: Export and re-import
options.detail: v1 exports JSONL (subject-access export format); v2 ingests it as fresh writes.
options.note: Loses event history and provenance timestamps unless carried explicitly.

why: The append-only log (BD-3, D0.1) exists so derived state can be rebuilt; RV05 requires that a replay of an old-key store creates no duplicates; a shim for one release keeps current callers (evals harness included) working while the API shape of G-16 lands.

title: Environment pinning for runs and installs
question: How should v2 pin the Python environment so that a shared install cannot silently change a run?
today: evals/pinned_run.sh (H7) pins the code in a detached worktree but runs in the shared .venv; on 2026-10-11 at 18:17 a uv sync re-installed the stale uv.lock (about 50 packages changed, huggingface_hub 1.16.1 below datasets' >=1.31), breaking five queued screens; the lock still pins 1.16.1 (uv.lock:1555) and was deliberately not regenerated (I69).
others: Mnemon: per-run commits and data checksums with byte-exact recompute. Hindsight: pinned benchmark harness version. Honcho: harness records full deriver/dialectic settings per run. Most engines publish no environment record.

options.label: Shared venv, fix lock by hand
options.detail: Today plus a one-off lock bump.
options.note: Next unrelated sync can break or silently change runs again.

options.label: Lock is truth, checked at run start
options.detail: Regenerate and commit a correct uv.lock; every pinned run verifies the installed set against the lock (uv sync --locked --check or a freeze hash) and refuses to start on drift.
options.note: Cheap; still one shared venv for all runs.

options.label: Per-run isolated environment
options.detail: Each pinned run creates its own venv from the lock in the worktree (uv cached, so seconds), records the freeze hash in the manifest, and never touches the shared venv.
options.note: Immune to concurrent syncs; more disk.

options.label: Container images per release
options.detail: Build an image per release with models and dependencies baked in.
options.note: Strongest reproducibility; GPU passthrough on Windows is awkward.

why: The 2026-10-11 incident shows code pinning without environment pinning is not a pinned run; uv makes per-worktree venvs cheap, and the freeze hash feeds the manifest of G-25. B is the minimum fallback.

title: Run manifest and comparability key
question: What must a v2 run manifest contain for two runs to count as comparable?
today: Result files carry resolved_system_config, protocol_digest, build_digest and environment (harness/memspine/python versions, git commit) (evals/README.md summary table); MEMSPINE_PINNED_COMMIT set by pinned_run.sh; G-E1 notes no frozen baseline manifest hash exists (V01); prompt hash, tokenizer, prefix-cache state and queue delay are not recorded (RV10).
others: Mnemon: collect.py recomputes results.json byte for byte from run records. Honcho: full deriver/dialectic/dream settings saved per run. LightMem: per-stage token, call and runtime accounting. MemOS: model versions pinned and context tokens reported.

options.label: Today's digests
options.detail: Config, protocol and build digests plus commit.
options.note: Misses environment freeze, prompt hashes, model files and dataset checksums.

options.label: Full manifest with hard match
options.detail: Add environment freeze hash, rendered prompt hashes per role, model and tokenizer identifiers with file hashes, dataset/split checksums, reader/judge settings, hardware and concurrency; the gate refuses a comparison whose manifests differ outside the declared changed field.
options.note: Makes 'paired against a named reference' checkable.

options.label: B plus recompute from raw outputs
options.detail: As B, and every headline number can be recomputed from stored per-item outputs by one command (no re-run), with the recompute hash in the manifest.
options.note: Paper-grade reproducibility; per-item files stay gitignored for licensed sets.

options.label: C plus cost and latency fields
options.detail: As C, with prefix-cache state, queue delay, retries, prompt/completion tokens and p50/p95 per stage under matched load.
options.note: Needed before any speed or token claim (RV10).

why: G-E1 requires pinned manifests; RV10 says no speed or token claim without prompt hash, tokenizer, cache state and queue delay; RV14 says snapshot claims need commit, data, reader, judge and budget. Licence hygiene (scores-only for OP-Bench) is kept by storing per-item outputs locally only.

title: Claims policy for the MemSpine paper
question: Which v2 results may the paper state as claims, and how are they scoped?
today: RESEARCH_NOVELTY.md carries N1-N7; N1 narrowed on 2 Oct 2026 (no open-source engine ships a poisoning defence with a proved cross-agent reach bound), with enforcement-on reruns still queued; LoCoMo dev-pool numbers and an errata file with both headlines exist; MAB-CR and ConvoMem blind runs not yet run; RV14/RV20 warn that survey cells are not verified implementations.
others: Mem0 and MemOS: headline numbers from hosted products, not the OSS code. EverMemOS: max over judge runs. Hindsight: unfilled token budget in the paper. Mnemon: reproducible but developed on the reported sets.

options.label: Report best measured numbers
options.detail: Quote the best development-pool scores with confidence intervals.
options.note: Same overfitting the survey criticises in peers.

options.label: Frozen-config blind numbers only
options.detail: Headline claims come only from the frozen configuration's single blind run (with manifest hash); dev-pool numbers are labelled development.
options.note: Lower headline, defensible.

options.label: B plus mechanism claims tied to loop metrics
options.detail: As B, and each novelty (N1-N7) is stated with its own evidence: N1 as an attack-success vs utility frontier with enforcement on, forgetting compliance and correction latency for the loop, cost per cycle with manifests; claims with no measurement are stated as design, not result.
options.note: Matches the framework paper's thesis (the loop, not a leaderboard).

options.label: Design claims only, no scores
options.detail: Position paper: constructs and engine as an instance, no benchmark claims.
options.note: Weak for TMLR, which expects evidence.

why: TMLR (D12) rewards claims matched to evidence; N1 needs the enforcement-on reruns and the attack/utility frontier; RV12, RV14 and RV20 require scoped, pinned claims; the loop metrics of G-05 are the evidence for the R->C coupling thesis.
